newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Supersol cut to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Supersol cut to hold.

text.p: ING Barings said on Monday it had downgraded its rating of Israel's Supersol Ltd, a food retailer, to a hold after reducing its 1997 earnings forecast to 0.60 shekel a share from 0.68 shekel.

"We expect earnings growth to be relatively modest this year, and the strong run-up in the share price since our last report on the stock provides an excellent opportunity for shareholders to take profits," analyst David Rey said.

Rey said Supersol's acquisition of the competing Shekem supermarket chain earlier this year had improved its competitiveness and reduced costs. However, he said, the acquisition left Supersol with added financial costs while the new outlets carry lower margins.
Rey said the company would also be stepping up capital expenditure this year to fund a domestic expansion drive.
"Supersol will revert from net cash in 1995/95 to net debt for the next five-year period. This will ratchet up financial expenses for the group," Rey said.
He said stronger profit growth would resume in 1998, when he forecasts earnings per share of 0.70 shekel.
